claims.text: An active-learning machine-learning potential with uncertainty quantification, adaptive sampling, and periodic on-the-fly ab initio corrections can accurately reproduce solid and liquid free-energy landscapes near melting.
The proposed framework can retain vibrational entropy in the calculated free energies.
The proposed framework can accurately capture anharmonic contributions to free energy.
The proposed framework can accurately capture electron–vibration coupling contributions.
The method is applicable to four- or five-element metallic high-entropy alloys within approximately ±10% of their melting points.
Moderate ab initio molecular-dynamics datasets containing both solid and liquid configurations are sufficient starting data for the method.
Local force Hessians, energy fluctuations, and uncertainty estimates can identify configurations requiring additional ab initio corrections.
Using these mediators for adaptive sampling will preserve local free-energy curvature, phonon spectra, and anharmonic potential-energy surfaces.
Configurations with high predicted uncertainty or significant deviations in local free-energy gradients will trigger ab initio recalculation and potential correction.
Selective correction of flagged configurations will reduce the need for exhaustive full-length ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations while preserving critical free-energy features.
The resulting phase free energies, melting temperatures, and entropy contributions will agree with explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics results to within approximately 5%.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by approximately 5–10 times relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by approximately 3–5 times relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will retain derived thermodynamic observables including latent heat and entropy jumps.
TOR-TILD has been validated on elemental and binary benchmark systems suitable for initial training or validation.
Sampling molecular-dynamics snapshots every 0.2–0.3 ps is an appropriate interval for the proposed free-energy integration workflow.
The approach can extend from elemental and binary systems to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Systems outside the ±10% melting-temperature range or with substantially more complex phase behavior may require modifications to the method.
